interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The textbook comparison is between two endpoint conformations shown side by side; the preview view adds motion only after the learner has seen what is being compared.

interactions.label: Rear-carbon rotation
interactions.teaches: A 60° rotation about the C-C bond moves the rear hydrogens from positions halfway between the front hydrogens into direct H/H alignment.
Each eclipsed H-H pair contributes the same 4.0 kJ/mol interaction, so the total eclipsing penalty is partitioned into three equal contributions.

demo_steps.title: Compare the two endpoints
demo_steps.narration: The default view preserves the source figure: staggered ethane is on the left, eclipsed ethane is on the right, and the arrow points from staggered to eclipsed. The key visual difference is that the staggered hydrogens alternate around the circle, while the eclipsed hydrogens occur in overlapping pairs.

demo_steps.title: Preview the rotation
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the rotation preview and move the rear-carbon rotation partway. Only the rear hydrogens move, showing that the two drawings differ by torsion about the C-C bond rather than by bond breaking.

demo_steps.title: Reach the eclipsed alignment
demo_steps.narration: At 60°, the rear bonds lie directly behind the front bonds. Returning to the endpoint comparison makes the three H/H overlaps and their three identical 4.0 kJ/mol labels easy to inspect.

plan.geometry_notes: Overall source-like layout is mandatory: two large panels side by side across the frame, not a single changing molecule. Use a fixed front-on perspective camera. World layout: left staggered panel centered at x=-3.0, right eclipsed panel centered at x=3.0, both y=0. The Newman projection in each panel sits slightly left within its panel, centered around x=-3.8 for the left panel and x=2.2 for the right panel, y=0.05. The ball-and-stick model sits slightly right within each panel, centered around x=-2.25 for the left panel and x=3.75 for the right panel, y=0.05. Keep the two panels similar size and aligned horizontally. Each Newman rear-carbon circle radius about 0.42 world units; front carbon dot radius 0.045. Front Newman C-H bonds extend from center to radius 0.70 and are thick black #000000, about 2.5 to 3 times the line width of rear bonds. Rear Newman bonds begin just outside or at the circle edge and extend to radius 0.74, thinner dark gray #222222. H label radius about 0.92. Front H labels are green #00a65a; rear H labels are magenta #ff1493. Staggered Newman front angles: 90°, 210°, 330°; rear angles: 30°, 150°, 270°, alternating evenly between front bonds. Eclipsed Newman front and rear angles: 90°, 210°, 330°; draw rear bonds just behind front bonds with a tiny radial or lateral offset only if needed for legibility, but visually they should read as overlapping. For each ball-and-stick model, orient the C-C bond almost exactly along the camera depth axis so the carbon skeleton appears end-on like the textbook model. Carbon spheres radius 0.17 to 0.20, dark gray #4f5a5d; front carbon may slightly occlude rear carbon. C-C distance about 0.75 to 0.90 along depth, with a short visible gray cylinder radius 0.035. Hydrogen spheres radius 0.13 to 0.15. C-H projected radial distance from the carbon center about 0.48 to 0.55 in screen space, with tetrahedral depth offsets kept subtle so the end-on ring is preserved. Front hydrogen spheres are green #2ecc71. Rear hydrogen spheres are red #b84032 or magenta-red #c23b32. In the staggered model, rear hydrogens occupy 30°, 150°, 270° so they alternate between the green front hydrogens. In the eclipsed model, rear hydrogens occupy 90°, 210°, 330° so red and green spheres appear as close coincident pairs; use a very small screen-space offset or partial transparency if exact overlap hides one color. The horizontal arrow spans the central gap from roughly x=-1.35 to x=1.35 at y=0.15, with arrowhead pointing right toward the eclipsed panel; label Rotate rear carbon 60° sits above the arrow at y=0.45 and is centered. Captions should be bold black, matching the source wording exactly: Ethane—staggered conformation and Ethane—eclipsed conformation. Place captions near the top or bottom consistently; avoid oversized UI labels competing with them. On the right Newman projection, braces are black and placed outside the H/H pairs: one above the top pair with its 4.0 kJ/mol label above or slightly to the side, one near the lower-left pair with its label below-left, and one near the lower-right pair with its label below-right. The three labels must all read exactly 4.0 kJ/mol. If the slider is used, rear angles are 30°+θ, 150°+θ, 270°+θ for the preview layer; θ=0 is staggered and θ=60 is eclipsed. Keep endpoint comparison visible by default; do not replace the original two-panel comparison with a single large dynamic conformation.
plan.notes: Render the Newman projections as flat screen-facing vector-like geometry in the Three.js scene or as a synchronized SVG overlay for crisp labels and line weights. Render each ball-and-stick model with sphere meshes and cylinder meshes, using an orthographic-feeling front-on perspective to avoid scale distortion. In Endpoint comparison mode, hide or minimize any angle readout, ghost geometry, narration panels, and extra highlights so the figure resembles the textbook source. In Rotation preview mode, reveal the slider-controlled rear-bond ghost or animate only a subtle overlay; keep the two endpoint panels as spatial references. The central arrow must remain between the two panels and point left-to-right from staggered to eclipsed. Click picking for highlightEclipsedPair should apply only to the three right-panel eclipsed pairs and their corresponding brace/label; clicking a pair should not add new explanatory callouts beyond the visual emphasis.

authoredPrompt: This figure compares two conformations of ethane, each shown as a Newman projection paired with a ball-and-stick model, with a reaction-style arrow between them. On the left, the Newman projection draws the front carbon as a dot at the center of a circle with three heavy bonds radiating up, down-left, and down-right to hydrogens lettered in green, while the rear carbon is the circle itself with three thinner bonds emerging at the left, right, and bottom to hydrogens lettered in magenta, so the two sets alternate evenly. Its ball-and-stick model, viewed end-on, shows a dark gray carbon ringed by three green and three red spheres in alternating positions. The horizontal arrow between the halves is labeled "Rotate rear carbon 60°". On the right, the projection shows each front bond lying directly over a rear bond, so the green and magenta hydrogens appear in overlapping pairs, and three curly braces, one at each pair, are each labeled "4.0 kJ/mol". The matching model now shows the green and red spheres in coincident pairs. Bold labels read "Ethane—staggered conformation" and "Ethane—eclipsed conformation". Setting the two projections side by side makes the hydrogen spacing the thing being compared, and the three equal energy labels partition the rotational barrier into individual eclipsing interactions.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rotating the rear carbon from 0 to 60 degrees; the Newman projection and ball-and-stick model update continuously from staggered to eclipsed, making torsional alignment the source of the conformational change.
- Click for highlighting one eclipsed H-H pair; its brace and 4.0 kJ/mol label brighten along with the overlapping hydrogens, clarifying how three identical interactions add to the rotational barrier.
authoredContext:
Despite what we’ve just said, we actually don’t observe perfectly free rotation in ethane. Experiments show that there is a small (12 kJ/mol; 2.9 kcal/mol) barrier to rotation and that some conformations are more stable than others. The lowest-energy, most stable conformation is the one in which all six C–H bonds are as far away from one another as possible—staggered when viewed end-on in a Newman projection. The highest-energy, least stable conformation is the one in which the six C–H bonds are as close as possible—eclipsed in a Newman projection. At any given instant, about 99% of ethane molecules have an approximately staggered conformation and only about 1% are near the eclipsed conformation.

Staggered conformation of ethane undergoes rotation of rear carbon 60 degrees to form eclipsed conformation of ethane.

The extra 12 kJ/mol of energy present in the eclipsed conformation of ethane is called torsional strain. Its cause has been the subject of controversy, but the major factor is an interaction between C–H bonding orbitals on one carbon and antibonding orbitals on the adjacent carbon, which stabilizes the staggered conformation relative to the eclipsed one. Because a total strain of 12 kJ/mol arises from three equal hydrogen–hydrogen eclipsing interactions, we can assign a value of approximately 4.0 kJ/mol (1.0 kcal/mol) to each single interaction. The barrier to rotation that results can be represented on a graph of potential energy versus degree of rotation, in which the angle between C–H bonds on the front and back carbons as viewed end-on (the dihedral angle) goes full circle from 0 to 360°. Energy minima occur at staggered conformations, and energy maxima occur at eclipsed conformations, as shown in the figure.
sourceQmd: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 3: Organic Compounds: Alkanes and Their Stereochemistry

interactions.label: Rotate rear carbon
interactions.teaches: The staggered and eclipsed conformations differ only by torsional rotation about the C-C bond; as the rear carbon turns, alternating hydrogens move into direct alignment.
Each eclipsed H-H overlap contributes the same 4.0 kJ/mol interaction, so the full barrier is the sum of three identical eclipsing interactions.

demo_steps.title: Staggered ethane
demo_steps.narration: At 0° the rear hydrogens sit halfway between the front hydrogens in the Newman projection. The ball-and-stick view shows the six hydrogens alternating around the C-C bond.

demo_steps.title: Rotating the rear carbon
demo_steps.narration: As the rear carbon rotates, the rear H labels and rear hydrogen spheres sweep around the C-C axis while the front carbon stays fixed. The changing Newman projection makes the torsional motion explicit.

demo_steps.title: Eclipsed ethane
demo_steps.narration: At 60° each rear C-H bond lies directly behind a front C-H bond. Three braces and three 4.0 kJ/mol labels identify the three equal eclipsed H-H interactions; click one pair to isolate a single contribution.

discrepancies: The ball-and-stick ethane models are too compressed and front-on compared with the source, with the carbon-carbon depth axis and individual rear/front carbons not as clearly visible.
The Newman projection and ball-and-stick model on the staggered side are placed too close together, causing the right-side Newman H labels to visually intrude on the molecular model.
The eclipsed interaction braces are approximate wavy curves and are less cleanly positioned around the three H-H eclipsing pairs than in the source.
The 3D molecular models have different proportions from the source, with hydrogens and bonds appearing slightly oversized relative to the carbon center.
Captions and some labels use translucent background boxes that are not present in the original textbook figure.
